## Answer: no, the repo ships zero agent-facing context

`crimes scan --format json` surfaces exactly one finding on this axis, and it's unambiguous:

**`crime_00011` — Missing Agent Context** (`missing_agent_context`, universal pack)
- severity `medium`, confidence `0.90`, **agent_risk `0.47`**
- effort: `small`

Evidence, verbatim from the scan:

```
no AGENTS.md found at repo root
no CLAUDE.md found at repo root
no .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md present
no .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md present
package.json declares bin(s): tsup, tsup-node — agents have no way to discover commands
```

One presentation note so you don't waste time: the finding is anchored to `assets/cjs_shims.js`, but it's a **repo-level** finding — the detector needs a `file` field and picked an arbitrary one. Nothing is wrong with `assets/cjs_shims.js`.

It's also worth noting where it lands in the ranking. At `agent_risk` 0.47 it sits **11th of 93** findings, above every `God Function` in the repo except three, despite being only `medium` severity. That's the aggregate-risk model working as intended: a missing context file has zero local severity but broad agent consequence.

## Why this matters for your first PR specifically

The scan gives you the receipts for what an uninstructed agent would get wrong here:

**1. You can't tell which files are load-bearing.** Four files are in the top connectivity tier and nothing in the repo says so:

| file | fan-in | fan-out |
|---|---|---|
| `src/utils.ts` | 18 | 1 |
| `src/plugin.ts` | 10 | 3 |
| `src/log.ts` | 9 | 0 |
| `src/index.ts` | 4 | 17 |

An agent asked to "clean up utils" will restructure a module 18 files import from, with no warning that it's a hub.

**2. Green tests won't mean what you think.** There are **21** `weak_test_signal` findings. Twelve of them contain **zero** `expect`/`assert` calls at all — `test/example.test.ts`, `test/graphql.test.ts`, `test/shims.test.ts`, and five in `test/experimental-dts.test.ts`. These tests only prove the build ran. An agent that changes behaviour, sees a green suite, and reports success is being actively misled. This is the single most important thing an AGENTS.md here could say.

**3. There's no discoverable command surface.** The package declares two bins (`tsup`, `tsup-node`) and the scan sees three manifests (`package.json`, `assets/package.json`, `test/package.json`) — so "which directory do I install and run in?" has a non-obvious answer, and nothing answers it.

**4. Names lie in the places you'd trust them.** `getRollupConfig` calls `setSilent` and `removeFiles`; `build` and `buildAll` both call `removeFiles`; `buildStart` deletes files. Four `False Identity` findings, all on read-or-transform-sounding names that mutate the filesystem. An agent treating `getRollupConfig` as a pure accessor will move or memoize a call that deletes output.

## Minimal AGENTS.md that clears the finding

The detector wants presence at the repo root — `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or a `SKILL.md` under `.claude/skills/` or `.agents/skills/`. `AGENTS.md` is the right pick: it's the cross-vendor convention, so one file serves Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor.

I've filled in what the scan actually establishes and marked the rest. **The `<!-- VERIFY -->` lines need checking against the real `package.json` scripts** — the scan reports declared bins, not scripts, so I can't confirm the exact invocations from JSON alone.

```markdown
# AGENTS.md

Build tool (esbuild + rollup for `.d.ts`). Node/TypeScript, single package
with nested manifests under `assets/` and `test/`.

## Commands

Run everything from the repo root.

<!-- VERIFY against package.json "scripts" before relying on these -->
- Install: `pnpm install`
- Build: `pnpm build`
- Test: `pnpm test`
- Typecheck: `pnpm typecheck`

## Before you edit

These files are load-bearing. Prefer additive changes; read the importers
before restructuring:

- `src/utils.ts` — 18 importers
- `src/plugin.ts` — 10 importers
- `src/log.ts` — 9 importers
- `src/index.ts` — imports 17 modules; the `build()` entry point

## Testing caveat — read this before reporting success

The suite is integration-style: tests shell out to a real build via the
`run()` helper in `test/utils.ts` and assert on emitted output.

**A green suite is weaker evidence than it looks.** Several tests contain no
assertions at all and only prove the build did not throw — including all of
`test/example.test.ts` and `test/graphql.test.ts`. If you change behaviour,
add a real assertion on the emitted output rather than relying on existing
coverage.

## Conventions

- Functions named `get*` / `build*` in this codebase may still perform file
  I/O — `getRollupConfig`, `build`, and `buildAll` all call `removeFiles`.
  Do not assume a read-sounding name is pure.
- Plugin `setup()` functions return several different object shapes by
  branch (esbuild plugin protocol). This is intentional, not a bug.

## Out of scope

<!-- VERIFY: replace with the project's real constraints -->
- Do not edit generated output under `dist/`.
- Do not change the public options shape in `src/options.ts` without a
  changeset.
```

Two follow-ups worth knowing:

- Adding this file clears `crime_00011` and nothing else — it does not touch the other 92 findings. It's a context fix, not a code fix.
- The "Testing caveat" section is the highest-value paragraph in the file. If you trim the skeleton, trim elsewhere. Twelve assertion-free tests is a trap that an agent will fall into on its first task and a human reviewer will not catch, because the CI badge will be green.
